titleText.es: Bien, está claro que el chaval va a heredar el fenotipo de friki biólogo.
titleText.en: Well, the kid's definitely getting the biology geek phenotype.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd source both identify comic #634. The archive translates the official title text's genetics joke.

regions.labelEs: MIS DOS PADRES ERAN DALTÓNICOS, ASÍ QUE...

applications.explanationEn: Así and que combine as the connector that leads from the parents' trait to a result or conclusion.

regions.labelEs: MIRA, SI TENEMOS MÁS DE DOS, TENEMOS MUCHAS OPCIONES DE CONSEGUIR UN ADORABLE PELO ROJO.

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces a genuinely possible condition, and tenemos uses the ordinary present form for the speaker's group.
Más de marks a numerical threshold being exceeded, and dos supplies that threshold.
Pelo names the feature first, and the neutral color description rojo follows it.
Rojo uses masculine singular -o to match the masculine singular noun pelo.

regions.labelEs: OOH, NO TE LO PIERDAS: ¡OJOS VERDES!

applications.explanationEn: No begins the instruction, te and lo come before the verb, and ordinary pierdes changes to the familiar negative-command form pierdas.
Te and pierdas form the pronominal action perderse, while lo stands for the noteworthy possibility not to miss.
Te marks the familiar person affected, lo identifies the thing, and both short pronouns stand before the changed verb pierdas in that order.
Ojos names the feature first, and the neutral color description verdes follows it.
Verdes adds plural -s to match ojos; verde has the same form with masculine and feminine nouns.

regions.labelEs: DATO: EL 30% DE LAS PRIMERAS CITAS ENTRE BIÓLOGOS DEGENERAN EN HACER CUADROS DE PUNNETT.

excludedUnits.rationale: 30% is a percentage measurement rather than a Spanish lexical word.
Punnett is the English surname in the scientific term, not a Spanish lexical word.

applications.explanationEn: Primeras appears before citas and uses feminine plural -as to match it.

applications.exampleEs: DEGENERAN EN HACER CUADROS DE PUNNETT
applications.explanationEn: Degeneran names the deterioration, en introduces the result, and hacer cuadros de Punnett supplies the resulting activity.

cards.promptEs: cuadro de Punnett · herencia de rasgos
cards.questionEn: What genetics idea connects the parents' traits, the imagined children, and the joke about the date?
cards.answerEn: A Punnett square is a grid used to show possible combinations of gene variants inherited from two parents. The couple treats possible children's visible traits like outcomes to optimize on a genetics worksheet.
cards.noteEn: Color-vision deficiency, hair color, and eye color have more complicated inheritance than a single simple grid can fully predict. The joke deliberately turns romantic conversation into an overconfident classroom genetics exercise.
Daltónicos describes more than one male or mixed-gender person who has color-vision deficiency.

cards.answerEn: so; therefore (as part of así que)

cards.questionEn: How do you connect a situation to its result with “so”?
cards.answerEn: Use así que before the result.
cards.noteEn: Así que joins a cause or situation to what follows from it. The two words work together as one connector; translating así and que separately will not give the intended meaning.

example.es: Está lloviendo, así que llevo un paraguas.
example.en: It is raining, so I am carrying an umbrella.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; part of a result connector
look; listen; hey (to get someone's attention)
cards.noteEn: Mira is the positive command form of mirar used with one familiar person. At the start of a comment, it often simply gets the listener's attention, like “look,” “listen,” or “hey,” without asking them to look at an object.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that an amount is more than a particular number or quantity?
cards.answerEn: Put más de directly before the number or amount.
cards.noteEn: Use más de when the next element is a quantity being exceeded. Use más que instead when directly comparing people, things, qualities, or actions: más de diez libros, but Ana lee más que Luis.

example.en: She bought more than three books.

cards.noteEn: Before a number or other quantity, Spanish uses más de for “more than.” This de is different from más que, which commonly compares one person, thing, or action with another.

example.en: There are more than twenty people.

cards.answerEn: to obtain; to work out; to achieve
cards.noteEn: Conseguir can mean obtaining a result through effort, not only physically getting an object.

example.en: We want to reach an agreement.

cards.noteEn: Adorable has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.
Pelo usually refers to hair collectively and is masculine.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.answerEn: ooh (a sound of sudden interest or excitement)
cards.noteEn: Ooh represents a drawn-out reaction rather than an ordinary dictionary noun or verb. Its tone can show delight, surprise, or sudden fascination.

cards.promptEs: orden negativa de tú: no + verbo
cards.questionEn: How do you tell one friend or familiar person not to do something?
cards.answerEn: Put no before the verb's special negative-command form. If the verb uses te, put te between no and the verb.
cards.noteEn: For a regular -ar verb, the negative form usually ends in -es: hablar becomes no hables. Regular -er and -ir verbs usually end in -as: comer becomes no comas. A short word such as te goes before this negative form, as in no te levantes.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word here; marks a “you” verb used with te
cards.noteEn: Some Spanish verbs use te when the person affected is the informal listener. The meaning belongs to the whole verb pattern, so English may not translate te separately.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone misses an event, opportunity, or part of an experience?
cards.answerEn: Use perder with a matching me, te, se, nos, or os marker, followed by the thing missed.
cards.noteEn: The marker changes with the person: me pierdo, te pierdes, se pierde, nos perdemos. Here perderse does not mean becoming geographically lost; it means failing to experience something.

example.en: I don't want to miss the concert.

cards.questionEn: How do you order a person pronoun and a thing pronoun before a verb that changes for person and time?
cards.answerEn: Put the person pronoun first, the thing pronoun second, and both before the changed verb.
cards.noteEn: The slashes mean to choose one item, and the plus signs show the order. For example, nos la mandará places nos for the recipients before la for the feminine thing. Before lo, la, los, or las, le and les change to se.

example.en: They will send it to us tomorrow.

cards.noteEn: Lo replaces a masculine singular thing, or sometimes a whole idea, as the direct object. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.

example.es: Tengo el libro y lo leo.
example.en: I have the book and I’m reading it.

cards.answerEn: miss out; miss it (in a negative informal command)
cards.noteEn: In no te lo pierdas, ordinary pierdes changes to pierdas because the speaker is telling one familiar person not to miss something.
Verde has one singular form for masculine and feminine nouns. Verdes adds -s to match a plural noun.
Dato can introduce a stated fact or statistic, as well as mean an individual piece of data.

cards.answerEn: of; or no separate English word, linking an amount to what it measures
cards.noteEn: After a quantity expression, de introduces the substance or thing being measured. English uses “of” in expressions such as a lot of or the amount of, but may leave de untranslated in others, such as un poco de agua, “a little water.”
Primeras matches a feminine plural noun.

cards.promptEs: número ordinal antes de un sustantivo
cards.questionEn: How do you use words such as first, second, or third before a Spanish noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the ordinal before the noun and make its ending match the noun's gender and number.
cards.noteEn: An ordinal gives a position in an order. Primero, segundo, tercero, último, and similar words usually come before the noun. Most forms use -o with a masculine singular noun and -a with a feminine singular noun, but primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun. Plural nouns use plural forms.

example.es: La segunda puerta está en el tercer piso.
example.en: The second door is on the third floor.

cards.noteEn: Cita can also mean an appointment or a quotation. Here citas are meetings between potential romantic partners.
Biólogos is the masculine or mixed-group plural for people who work in biology.

cards.answerEn: degenerate; deteriorate; turn into something worse
cards.noteEn: Degeneran is the present plural form of degenerar. With en, it names the undesirable result that situations turn into.

cards.questionEn: How can you say that a situation deteriorates or turns into an undesirable result?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of degenerar followed by en and the resulting situation.
cards.noteEn: Degenerar changes for the person or thing and the time: degenera now, degeneró in a completed past event. En stays fixed and introduces the worse or less controlled result.

cards.answerEn: into; introduces the result after degenerar
cards.noteEn: Degenerar en presents what a situation deteriorates or turns into.

example.es: La charla degeneró en una pelea.
example.en: The conversation degenerated into a fight.

cards.noteEn: Hacer can mean creating or producing a physical thing. This is distinct from its very common sense “to do.”

example.en: We are going to make a table.

cards.noteEn: Cuadro can mean a square, chart, frame, or painting. In genetics, cuadro de Punnett is the Spanish name for a Punnett square.

example.es: La clase dibujó un cuadro de Punnett.
example.en: The class drew a Punnett square.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”
